advances: Chooses an auxiliary scale when compact attainment and two-sided value bounds already hold.
author: PK-research-agent
proof: The trial $\varepsilon=\tau/C$ and the upper value bound give infimum at most $\beta_*+\tau-\tau\log(\tau/C)$, which is below $b$ for sufficiently small $\tau$. Since $\bar\varepsilon\le1$, the penalty is nonnegative and a minimizing sequence is in the original strict sublevel. At fixed $\tau$ the penalty tends to infinity as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, whereas $\beta_\varepsilon\ge0$. Joint continuity on the compact representative class at scales bounded away from zero gives attainment. For a minimizer write $\varepsilon=\tau s$. The lower value bound and the trial imply $c_1 s-\log s\le1+\log C$, so $s$ stays in a fixed compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$, giving the interior assertion. A minimizer must minimize the body value at its chosen scale since its penalty then is constant.
statement: Assume the compact-sublevel setting and the fixed-scale value inequalities $\beta_*+c_1\varepsilon\le\inf_K\beta_\varepsilon(K)\le\beta_*+C\varepsilon$ of the body-tied attainment theorem. Choose $0<\bar\varepsilon\le1$ in their range. For all sufficiently small $\tau>0$, the infimum of $\beta_\varepsilon(K)-\tau\log\varepsilon$ over all positive compatible families on $P$ and $0<\varepsilon\le\bar\varepsilon$ is attained. Every minimizer is an attained body minimum at its scale, with $\varepsilon/\tau$ bounded above and below by positive constants independent of small $\tau$, hence with interior scale.
title: Interior logarithmic scale selection for the body-tied buffer
